description: Shared word-boosting test vectors, version 1 (docs/dictionary/DESIGN.md section 1 plus docs/dictionary/DESIGN-pins.md P1-P5). All text is invented. Consumed by Rust (linux/crates) and Swift (Tests/DictionaryTests.swift).

Strings are Unicode scalar sequences. Non-ASCII scalars are written as JSON \u escapes so combining marks stay visible. Compare strings scalar by scalar, never with canonical equivalence (Swift: compare unicodeScalars).
constants: alpha, context_score and depth_scaling of section 1.2; blank is the blank row; verify_strengths are tried in this order (section 1.6).

vocab: synthetic pieces in rank order; the array index is the token id and the merge rank (lower merges first). Index 0 is <unk>, which encoding never produces as a merge. Build a test tokenizer straight from this list.

encode: {text, tokens}. Section 1.3: prefix U+2581, replace each ASCII space (only U+0020) with U+2581, one symbol per scalar, repeatedly merge the adjacent pair whose concatenation is the piece with the lowest id (leftmost pair on ties), then map symbols to ids; a maximal run of consecutive symbols that are not pieces becomes a single <unk> (P4). The empty string still gets the prefix, so it encodes as U+2581 alone (P7).

validation: {text, strength?, ok, normalized?, error?}. Strength defaults to 1.0. Steps in this order, the first failure wins: empty (no words after trimming Unicode White_Space), too-many-words (> 8), too-long (> 100 scalars after collapsing whitespace runs to one ASCII space), no-letter (no general category L*), unencodable (the normalized text encodes with <unk>; a control character (Cc) is never a piece, so it always fails here, P6), bad-strength (not finite or outside [0.25, 8.0]).

phrases: {name, entries:[{text, strength}], phrases:[{surface, tokens, strength}]}. The token sequences an entry list boosts (section 1.2 surfaces: text, fold, upper1, each word upper1; surfaces with <unk> skipped; duplicate sequences keep the largest strength), listed sorted by token sequence (lexicographic on ids). surface is informative.

graph: {name, phrases:[{tokens, strength}], steps:[{path, token, bonus}]}. Build the graph over 1024 tokens, walk path from the root (-1 is blank: no state change), then the bonus of token from that state must equal bonus within 1 ULP of f32. Expected values are exact f64 math (sigma as f64 of the f32 strength) cast to f32. G1-G5 are the hand-computed DESIGN cases.

decision: {name, phrases, path, logits, expected_token}. Rows 0..=1024 (1024 = blank); logits lists the non-default rows (f32), every other row is -100.0. Walk path, then argmax over rows of f64(logit) + f64(bonus) with blank's bonus 0; the first maximum wins.

casing: {entries (texts), transcript, expected}: section 1.4 casing restoration (apply to the original transcript, left to right, longest entry first then entry text in scalar order, fold equality by scalars, word-character boundaries L* M* Nd Pc, no rescanning; lowercase-only entries are inert).

candidates: {before, after, dictionary (entry texts), ignore (identity keys), expected:[{surface, kind, before_range, before_words}]}: section 1.5 with P1/P2. before_range is a half-open range of indices into before's whitespace-separated words (words whose norm is empty keep their index but are not aligned); before_words are the norms of the block's before words. Dictionary entries have strength 1.0; candidates are validated with the vocab above.

verify: {name, B, before, after, candidate_index, N_by_strength, expected_strength}: compute the candidates of (before, after) with an empty dictionary and ignore list, take candidate_index; a casing candidate is accepted at 1.0 with no audio. Otherwise, for each strength in verify_strengths order, N is N_by_strength[strength] (keys are written 1.0, 1.41, 2.0, 2.83, 4.0, 5.66, 8.0; a missing key means N = B), and verify_decision(B, before, candidate, N) per section 1.6 with P2/P3; expected_strength is the first strength accepted, or null. Verification order across several candidates (P8: unattempted ones dropped before the cap of 3, budget rechecked after each decode) is tested by each platform with a mocked clock.

keys: {key, valid, from?}: DESIGN P6. A stored identity or ignore key is valid iff it is non-empty, has at most 300 scalars and at most 8 words separated by U+0020, has no control character (Cc), and fold(key) == key. With from, fold(from) must equal key (folding can expand: a valid 100-scalar entry may have a 101-scalar key, which must save and load unchanged).
